questions.question: In February 2021, In which of the following cases did the Court observe that the consent of a family is not needed once two adults decide to marry?

options.text: Satbir Singh v. State of Haryana
Rahul Sharma v. National Insurance Company Ltd.
Devilal v. State of Madhya Pradesh
Laxmibai Chandaragi v. The State of Karnataka

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Laxmibai Chandaragi v. The State of Karnataka.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Laxmibai Chandaragi B v. State of Karnataka(2021)** - **Upholding the Personal Liberty**.

 
 
• The Indian Supreme Court rendered a landmark decision in the Laxmibai Chandaragi B v. State of Karnataka(2021) and others case, upholding the basic right under** Article 21** of the Constitution to choose one's life mate.
 
• The court stressed that a person's decision on marriage should not be influenced by caste, social conventions, or family approval.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satbir Singh v. State of Haryana** - **related to dowry death**.

 
 
• Supreme court mentioned 12 guidelines related to dowry death
 
• The meaning of "soon before death" was clarified by the Supreme Court. It provided the trial court with guidelines stating that "soon before her death" does not imply that the court should remember that there should be a proper relationship between dowry death and cruelty for dowry asked by the husband or relatives just before the death of a woman.
 
 
 
• **Rahul Sharma Vs National Insurance Company Ltd (2021)** - 
 
 
• The case challenges the modified compensation part of a previous judgment of the High Court of Delhi.
 
• 
 
This judgment stated that she will be liable for 40% of future prospects in her income even though she is self-employed.

 
 
 
 
• **Devilal vs. State of Madhya Pradesh - Prevention of Untouchability**
 
 
• The Devilal v. State of MP case is significant because it centers on an Untouchability occurrence. Untouchability is a wicked practice that has been practiced in both rural and some urban regions from ancient times.

questions.question: Which of the following organic compounds is synonymous with olefiant gas which is used to make anaesthetics, refrigerants and other chemicals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ethylene**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ethylene, also known as the ripening hormone plays a role in plant growth.
 
• Ethylene appears as a **colorless gas with a sweet odor and taste**.
 
• It is lighter than air.
 
• Ethylene is used in used to make **anaesthetics, refrigerants and other chemicals**.
 
• It is also an important natural plant hormone and is used in agriculture to force the ripening of fruits.
 
• The **hydrate of ethylene is ethanol**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Methane**

 
• This compound contains 1 carbon atom which is indicated by writing 'meth'.
 
• This compound has all single bonds, so it is saturated.
 
• The saturated hydrocarbon is indicated by the ending 'ane'.
 
• On joining 'meth' and 'ane', the IUPAC name of its compound becomes,' 'methane'.
 
• The molecular formula of methane is CH4.
 
• Thus, the IUPAC name as well as the common name of the hydrocarbon CH4 is the same, methane. 
 
• It is an Alkane and its general formula is CnH2n+2.

​**Butane**

 
• Butane is one of two saturated hydrocarbons, or alkanes, with the chemical formula C4H10 of the paraffin series. In both compounds, the carbon atoms are joined in an open chain. In *n*-butane the chain.
 
• Butane derivatives are highly flammable, colorless, easily liquefied gases that quickly vaporize at room temperature.
 
• IUPAC Nomenclature of Butane is (CH3CH2CH2CH3).
 
• Butane is added to the gasoline and increases its volatility in cold climates. Transformed to isobutane in a refinery process known as isomerization, it can be reacted with certain other hydrocarbon derivatives such as butane to form valuable high-octane constituents of gasoline.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a tributary of the Godavari river?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mahi rises in Madhya Pradesh and, after flowing through the Vagad region of Rajasthan, enters Gujarat and flows into the Arabian Sea.
 
• Mahi River is the only river in India that cuts the Tropic of Cancer twice, first in Madhya Pradesh then it flows towards Rajasthan and enters Gujarat where it cuts for the second time.
 
• It is bounded by Aravalli hills on the north and the north-west, by Malwa Plateau on the east, by the Vindhyas on the south, and by the Gulf of Khambhat on the west.
 
• It originates from the northern slopes of Vindhyas at an altitude of 500m in the Dhar district of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It drains into the Arabian Sea through the Gulf of Khambhat.
 
• Hydro Power stations are located in Mahi Bajaj Sagar dam and at Kadana Dam.
 
• Vadodara is the only important urban center in the basin.
 
• Mahi is **not **the tributary of Godavari.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Godavari river is the largest river of Peninsular India. 
 
• It is the second longest river of the country with length 1465 km.
 
• The old name of Godavari river was Vriddh (Old) Ganga or the Dakshin (South) Ganga.
 
• It originates from Maharashtra.
 
• Trbutaries of Godavari are - the Pravara, the Purna, the Manjra, the Penganga, the Wardha, the Wainganga, the Pranhita the Indravati, the Maner and the Sabri.
 
• longest tributary - Manjira.
 
• largest tributary - Pranahita.

questions.question: What is the significance of 26 January being chosen as a day to celebrate the Republic Day, aside from the adoption of the constitution?

options.text: Foundation day of the Indian National Congress

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** **____**Declaration of Purna Swaraj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Significance of 26 January being chosen as a day to celebrate Republic Day, aside from the adoption of the constitution as the day Indian National Congress (INC) issued the Declaration of Indian Independence in 1930,
 
• The day was chosen since it was the day that the Poorna Swaraj resolution of the Congress was adopted.
 
• Republic Day is observed nationwide on January 26, 1950, the day the Constitution became operative.
 
• This day marked the beginning of India's ancient civilization, a mashup of several cultures and kingdoms. ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Champaran Satyagraha (April 1917):

 
 
• It was the first Satyagraha movement led by Gandhi in the Champaran district of Bihar.
 
• The Issue was Indigo Cultivation under the Tinkathia System ((3/20)th of total land).
 
• Gandhi convinced the authorities to end the system
 
• Demand was accepted and 25% compensation was given.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress**
 
 
• The Indian National Congress was formed in 1885 by A.O. Hume, an Englishman, and a retired civil servant.
 
• Indian National Congress was established in 1885.
 
• The first session of INC was held at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskriti College in Bombay.
 
• It was presided over by Womesh Chandra Banerjee of Bengal and attended by 72 delegates.
 
• W.C. Banerjee was one of the first-ever Indian barristers and one of the foremost legal luminaries of the day, his election established a healthy precedent that the president should be chosen from a province other than the one in which the Congress was being held.

questions.question: During the reign of Akbar, _________ was the land that has lain fallow for three or four years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chachar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Mughal Emperor Akbar made a few experiments in the land revenue administration with the help of Raja Todar Mal.
 
• The land revenue system of Akbar was called the Zabti system.
 
• During Akbar's reign, all the agricultural land was classified into four divisions:
 
 
• Polar
 
• Parati
 
• Chachar
 
• Banjar
 
 
 
• Polaj land was always cultivated and never left fallow.
 
• The Parauti land was left fallow for a year or two to retain its fertility.
 
• **Chachar land was left uncultivated for three or four years**.
 
• Banjar land was left fallow for five or more years.
 
• Polaj and Parauti were further subdivided into three categories: good, middle and bad.
 
• The average of these three called Mahsul was taken as a normal produce per bigha.

questions.question:
Which of the following can be considered as an example of flow variable?

(i) Production of rice

(ii) Import of cloth

(iii) Change in capital
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** **____**All of (i), (ii) and (iii)**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A flow is a quantity that is measured with reference to a period of time.
 
• Thus, flows are defined with reference to a specific period (length of time).
 
• National income is a flow.
 
• It describes and measures flow of goods and services which become available to a country during a year.
 
• Example of flow variable are Production of rice, Import of cloth and Change in capital.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Stock Variable**

__
 
• Stocks are defined at a particular point in time.

 
 
• So,__ Wealth is a stock variable as it can be measured at a particular time. 
 
 
 
• A flow shows change during a period of time whereas a stock indicates the quantity of a variable at a point of time.
 
• Wealth is a stock since it can be measured at a point of time.
 
• Income is a flow because it can be measured over a period of time.
 
• Salary and change in wealth is a flow because it can be measured over a period of time.

• Purulia Chhau - West Bengal
 
• Mayurbanj Chhau - Odisha
 
• Seraikella Chhau - Jharkhand
 
 

 
• Chhau Dance is a popular form of tribal dance in India that incorporates elements of martial arts into its movements.
 
• Differences between the three are dependent on their regions of origin.
 
• This Dance originates in the Purulia district in West Bengal and draws inspiration from martial arts and combative training.
 
• This form of dance is a means to portray stories to the audience, which is why elaborate masks and headgear associated with battle and war are worn during the performance.
 
• It enacts episodes from epics including the Mahabharata and Ramayana, local folklore, and abstract themes.
 
• Over a century old, this dance form was widely endorsed by patrons belonging to the royal families, rich landlords, and British governors in the region.
 
• These performances are predominantly put up during the Gajan Festival, which takes place to honor Lord Shiva.

questions.question: Who among the following freedom fighters lost his life during the protest against Simon Commission where black flags were waved at the Commission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lala Lajpat Rai**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Lala Lajpat Rai:

__
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai immensely contributed to attaining the independence of the nation.
 
• Besides, a great freedom fighter and leader, Lala Lajpat Rai was also a noted writer.
 
• He died after the police lathi-charged on the activists, protesting the arrival of Simon Commission. 
 
• On October 30, 1928, to boycott the arrival of the members of the Simon Commission in Lahore, a peaceful procession, headed by Lajpat Rai was launched.
 
• Intercepting the march, Superintendent of Police, Scott ordered his police force to ’lathi-charge at the activists.
 
• To take avenge the death of Lala Lajpat Rai, Bhagat Singh and his associates plotted the assassination of Scott.
 
• But, the revolutionaries, mistaking J.P. Saunders, an Assistant Superintendent of Police, as Scott, killed him instead.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Chittaranjan Das

 
• He was born on 5th November 1869 in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
 
• He was popularly called Deshbandhu which means friend of the country. 
 
• He was an Indian politician and leader of the Swaraj (Independence) Party in Bengal under British rule.
 
• He was a leading figure in Bengal during the Non-Cooperation Movement of 1919-1922.
 
• He initiated the ban on British clothes, setting an example by burning his own European clothes and wearing khadi clothes.
 
• He successfully defended Aurobindo Ghosh in the Alipore bomb case.
 
• He brought out a newspaper called ‘Forward’ and later changed its name to ‘Liberty’ to fight the British Raj.

**​Sachindra Nath Sanyal**

 
• Sanyal was considered the most senior leader of India's revolutionary movement after Subhash Chandra Bose escaped to Japan. 
 
• Sanyal was also jailed for his involvement in the Kakori conspiracy but he was later released.
 
• Sachindra Nath was also a mentor for revolutionaries like Chandrashekhar Azad and Bhagat Singh.
 
• He contracted tuberculosis in jail and was sent to Gorakhpur Jail for his final months.
 
• He died on 7 February 1942.

**​Surendranath Banerjee**

 
• Sir Surendranath Banerjee often known as Rashtraguru was an Indian nationalist leader during British Rule.
 
• He founded a nationalist organization called the Indian National Association and was one of the founding members of the Indian National Congress.
 
• Surendranath supported Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms, unlike Congress, and with many liberal leaders he left Congress and founded a new organization named Indian National Liberation Federation in 1919.
 
• Surendranath Banerjee was born in Calcutta, in the province of Bengal to a Rarhi Kulin Brahmin family, suggesting that the ancestral seat of the family was in the Rarh region of present-day West Bengal.

questions.question: In Which year did John Newlands propound the 'Law of Octaves' an innovative concept proposing the periodicity of chemical elements arranged in the order of atomic weight?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1865.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The '**Law of Octaves' was propounded by the English chemist J.A.R. Newlands in 1865**.
 
• The '**Law of Octaves'states that if the chemical elements are arranged according to increasing atomic weight, those with similar physical and chemical properties occur after each interval of seven elements.**
 
• **J.A.R. Newlands was the first to disclose a periodic pattern in the properties of the elements and anticipated late**r developments of the periodic law.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

There were the following limitations of the Newland's Law of Octaves

 
• It was found that the Law of Octaves was applicable only up to calcium, as after calcium every eighth element did not possess properties similar to that of the first.
 
• It was assumed by Newlands that only 56 elements existed in nature and no more elements would be discovered in the future. But, later on, several new elements were discovered, whose properties did not fit into the Law of Octaves.
 
• After the discovery of the Noble gases, the Law of Octaves became irrelevant. Thus, Newlands’ Law of Octaves worked well with lighter elements only.

questions.question: The finance commission of India is required to make recommendations to the __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President of India**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Finance Commissions are commissions periodically constituted by the President of India under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution to define the financial relations between the central government of India and the individual state governments.

 
 
• Its core responsibility is to:

 
 
• Evaluate the state of finances of the Union and State Governments
 
• Recommend the sharing of taxes between them
 
• Lay down the principles determining the distribution of these taxes among States.
 
 
 
 
 
• The Finance Commission is required to make **recommendations to the President of India.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Functions of the Finance Commission:

 
 
• The distribution of the net proceeds of taxes to be shared between the Centre and the states, and the allocation between the states of the respective shares of such proceeds.
 
• The principles that should govern the grants-in-aid to the states by the Centre (i.e. out of the consolidated fund of India).
 
• The measures needed to augment the consolidated fund of a state to supplement the resources of the panchayats and the municipalities in the state on the basis of the recommendations made by the state finance commission.
 
• Any other matter referred to it by the president in the interests of sound finance.
 
 
 
• Composition of the Finance commission:
 
 
• The Finance Commission consists of a chairman and four other members to be appointed by the President.
 
• They hold office for five years as specified by the president in his order. They are eligible for reappointment.
 
• The Constitution authorise the Parliament to determine the qualifications of members of the commission and the manner in which they should be selected.
 
• Accordingly, the Parliament has specified the qualifications of the chairman and members of the commission.
 
 
• The chairman should be a person having experience in public affairs.
 
• The four other members should be selected from amongst the following:
 
 
• A judge of a high court or one qualified to be appointed as one.
 
• A person who has specialized knowledge of finance and accounts of the government.
 
• A person who has wide experience in financial matters and in administration.
 
• A person who has special knowledge of economics.

questions.question: Aditi Mangal Das was conferred the Mahari Award for dance in 2022 for which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Kathak**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathak dancer** and choreographer** Aditi Mangaldas **was born in 1960.
 
• She is renowned for her repertoire in both classical Kathak and "**contemporary dance based on kathak**."
 
• **Mangaldas** is regarded as one of the best Kathak dancers in the world, both in India and outside.
 
• She has won numerous awards for her notable contributions in Kathak including the National Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2013. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Kathak:**

 
• The well-known ancient Indian classical dance known as Kathak is said to have originated with the **nomadic storytellers from North India known as Kathakars**.
 
• These Kathakars traveled and told tales using songs, dances, and music that were reminiscent of classical Greek theatre.
 
• The foundations of Kathak are rooted in Natya Shastra, an ancient Sanskrit text written by Bharata Muni.
 
• **The three chief sections of a Kathak dance are:**
 
 
• **Invocation**: The act of an artist offering a prayer or salutation to God and their guru is known as an invocation.
 
 
• Hindu performers employ mudras, or hand gestures, to convey the same message.
 
• On Muslim holidays, the artist presents a "salami."
 
 
 
• **Nritta**: The artist's portrayal of pure dancing.
 
 
• He or she begins by moving the neck, wrists, and eyebrows slowly and elegantly.
 
• The quick sequences according to "bols" come next. A bol is a brief rhythmic pattern sequence. Here, the artist also demonstrates lively footwork.
 
 
 
• **Nritya**: In this piece, the performer uses facial expressions, slow body motions, and vocal and instrumental music to tell a tale or explore a theme.

questions.question: The North-South corridor links which of the two major cities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Srinagar and Kanyakumari.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** North-South Corridor** is one of the key components of the **National Highways Development Project (NHDP).**
 
• It involves the development of a high-quality road network that connects the northern and southern parts of India.
 
• The corridor typically starts** from Srinagar** in the north and extends down **to Kanyakumari in the south.**
 
• The primary objective of the North-South Corridor is to enhance connectivity, reduce travel time, and facilitate the smooth movement of goods and people between different regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **East-West Corridor** is a part of **NHDP Phase-II**. It involves the development of a high-quality road network connecting the eastern and western regions of India.

 
 
• The corridor typically spans **from Porbandar in Gujarat** on the western coast **to Silchar in Assam **on the eastern border.
 
 
 
• The **Golden Quadrilateral (GQ)** is a significant highway network in India and one of the key components of the National Highways Development Project (NHDP). 
 
 
• The primary objective of the Golden Quadrilateral project is to create a high-quality** road network linking the four major metropolitan cities of India,** forming a quadrilateral shape.
 
• The cities included in the quadrilateral are **Delhi (North)**, **Mumbai (West)**, **Chennai (South)**, and **Kolkata (East**).
 
• The first phase, covering the main routes connecting the four cities, was **initiated in 2001.**

questions.question: Who among the following gave the famous 'Do or Die' slogan during Quit India Movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Mahatma Gandhi__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi gave the** famous 'Do or Die' slogan during the Quit India Movement.** 
 
• The Quit India Movement was a significant movement **launched **by the Indian National Congress **on August 8, 1942**, demanding an end to British rule in India.
 
• The** 'Do or Die'** slogan emphasized the urgency and determination of the Indian people to achieve independence. 
 
• Gandhiji is known as the Father of our Nation.
 
• He returned to India from South Africa on 9th January 1915 and celebrated it as **Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (NRI Day)**.
 
• The first satyagraha of Gandhiji is Chamapran Satyagraha (1917) also known as the first civil disobedience movement.
 
• The first hunger strike of Gandhiji is Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918).
 
• The first non-cooperation movement of Gandhiji is Kheda Satyagraha (1918).
 
• He was the president of the INC session in Belgaum (1924).
 
• In 1931, Gandhiji participated in the Second Round Table Conference in London.
 
• Gandhiji was assassinated on 30 January 1948 by Nathuram Godse and observed as 'Martyrs Day'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Abul Kalam Azad** 

 
 
• He was the first Education Minister of India.
 
• He also contributed to the establishment of educational institutes like Jamia Millia Islamia and IIT Kharagpur.
 
• He strongly advocated education for women and free and compulsory primary education for children up to the age of 14.
 
• He was awarded with Bharat Ratna in 1992 posthumously.
 
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru**
 
 
• He was the first prime minister of India and was one of the most prominent leaders of the Indian independence movement.
 
• Jawaharlal succeeded **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, who was President in 1928-1929.
 
• His father Motilal Nehru was an Indian lawyer, activist and politician belonging to the Indian National Congress.
 
• He also served as the Congress President twice, 1919–1920 and 1928–1929.
 
• He was a patriarch of the Nehru-Gandhi family and the father of Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of India.
 
 
 
• **Subhash Chandra Bose**
 
 
• He was born on 23rd January 1897, in Cuttack, Orissa Division, Bengal Province.
 
• The birth anniversary of Netaji on 23rd January is celebrated as 'Parakram Diwas'.
 
• He is popularly known as 'Netaji'.
 
• He passed the Indian Civil Services Examination in 1920 in England but left it on Gandhiji's call of the Non-cooperation Movement.
 
• He was the first elected INC President at the Haripura Session in 1938 and Tripuri Session in 1939.
 
• He founded the Forward Bloc in 1939 and Kisan Sabha.
 
• The first division of INA was formed in September 1942 with the help of Japan.

questions.question: The national poverty line for 2011-12 was estimated at _________ per capita per month for urban areas of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rs. 1,000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to an** International Monetary Fund** paper, **extreme poverty**, **defined by the World Bank as living on US$1.9 or less in purchasing power parity** (PPP) terms.
 
• According to the Planning Commission in 2011-12, the national poverty line using Tendulkar methology is** Rs 816 per capita per month for rural areas** and **Rs 1000 per capita per month for urban areas of India**. 
 
• The current poverty line is 1,059.42 Indian Rupees per month in rural areas and 1,286 Indian rupees per month in urban areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** POVERTY MEASUREMENT IN INDIA:

 
• Poverty can be defined as a condition in which an individual or household lacks the financial resources to afford a basic minimum standard of living.
 
• India has a long history of studies on measurement of poverty. The erstwhile Planning Commission was the nodal agency in India for estimation of poverty.
 
• Various expert groups constituted by the Planning Commission have estimated the number of people living in poverty in India:
 
 
• Working Group (1962).
 
• Study by VM Dandekar and N Rath (1971).
 
• Task Force on “Projections of Minimum Needs and Effective Consumption Demand” headed by Dr. Y. K. Alagh (1979).
 
• Lakdawala Expert Group (1993): Headed by Professor D.T. Lakdawala.
 
• Tendulkar Expert Group (2009): It was setup in 2005 and was headed by Suresh Tendulkar.
 
• Rangrajan Committee (2014): It was set up in 2012 and was headed by Chakravarthi Rangarajan.
